units.title: Myths, legends and stories that inspire
units.description: In this unit, pupils read and explore a range of text types in connection to classical myths and legends. They first look at poetry before doing some descriptive writing inspired by poetry and paintings. They then explore Chaucer and modern retellings of myths to inspire their narrative writing.

lessons.title: Bruegel's Landscape with the Fall of Icarus: how the myth inspired the painting
lessons.outcome: I can explain how Pieter Bruegel’s painting 'Landscape with the Fall of Icarus' was inspired by a Greek myth.
keyLearningPoints: Greek myths are stories originally told by the ancient Greeks as a way of explaining the origin and nature of the world.
Sometimes Greek myths contain morals.
The moral of the Fall of Icarus is that hubris is dangerous.
Pieter Bruegel’s 'Landscape with the Fall of Icarus' (c. 1558) was inspired by the Greek myth.
Bruegel’s painting celebrates the humility of labourers by making them the focus of the painting.

keywords.definition: stories which explain how the world began and what the world is like and why
excessive pride
being modest, humble, the opposite of hubristic
to be filled with the desire and motivation to do something
a lesson, often about how to behave, taught through a story

equipment: Pupils will need access to an image of Pieter Bruegel's 'Landscape with the Fall of Icarus' (c. 1558).

contentGuidance.label: Depiction or discussion of sensitive content
contentGuidance.description: Subjects which particular individuals may be sensitive to, eg, adoption, migration, bereavement or death, divorce, poverty, deprivation.

starterQuiz.stem: Creative people – writers, painters, sculptors etc. – are often inspired by other pieces of art they have read, seen, listened to or heard of. What does it mean to be inspired?
starterQuiz.hint: Consider that to be inspired is a positive idea.
starterQuiz.feedback: The feeling of being inspired is exciting. Often, a piece of art, or a text, can spark something in the imagination to help with the creative process. This is why it's so important to read, hear, watch and experience lots of different type of art.

options.text: to copy someone else's work but put it in a different format
to mimic someone else's work and referring to them throughout
to be motivated to create something after experiencing someone else's work
to compare your work to someone else's and explain the differences

starterQuiz.stem: In the unit 'Myths, legends and stories that inspire', we are going to read a story in which Greece, Athens and Crete are important locations. Match each place to a fact about it.
starterQuiz.hint: Consider that Greece is the largest of all these places.
starterQuiz.feedback: Greece is famous for many different things, but one of them is a type of story called a myth. One of the most famous is about a man called Daedalus who has to leave Athens and live in Crete.

match.left: a country in southeastern Europe
a large island in the Mediterranean sea
a capital city

starterQuiz.stem: In 'Myths, legends and stories that inspire', we explore a story called the Fall of Icarus, a famous Greek myth. What is a myth?
starterQuiz.hint: Consider that myths often contain supernatural events.
starterQuiz.feedback: Many different cultures have their own myths and mythologies. The myths differ widely, but share some common features. For example, explaining how the world began, or certain social customs. They often involve supernatural characters or events.

options.text: a story telling people how to behave
a truthful account of the history of a nation
a story often explaining what the world is like and why

starterQuiz.stem: In the unit 'Myths, legends and stories that inspire', we will look at a range of different stories. There are so many different ways to tells stories. Match each text type to its definition.
starterQuiz.hint: Consider one or more poems that you have read or written. What do they look like on the page?
starterQuiz.feedback: Myths, legends, poems and paintings have a rich history in almost all cultures. You have probably read, watched, seen or listened to examples of all of them.

match.left: stories which explain how the world began and what the world is like
a story about humans, often seeming historical but still fictitious
a piece of writing written in stanzas and with a close focus on rhythm
a visual art in which colour and brushes are used to convey meaning

starterQuiz.stem: Some texts you will read in the unit 'Myths, legends and stories that inspire' will include morals. What is a moral?
starterQuiz.hint: Consider that an example of a moral is treat others as you wish to be treated.
starterQuiz.feedback: Stories with morals are often read with and to children to teach them right from wrong in a way that is engaging.

options.text: a lesson taught through the act of story-telling
a story deriving from ancient Greece
a piece of non-fiction giving instructions

starterQuiz.stem: Some of the stories in 'Myths, legends and stories that inspire' inspire artwork. For example, Pieter Bruegel painted a picture in around 1558 inspired by a myth. What is true of the year 1558?
starterQuiz.hint: Consider that the Victorian era was named after Queen Victoria who was Queen of Britain from 1819 to 1901.
starterQuiz.feedback: Pieter Bruegel was born in the Netherlands in around 1525. One of his most famous paintings was inspired by a Greek myth and painted in 1558, the 16th century.

options.text: It is the time of ancient Greek civilisation.
It is part of the 16th century.
It is part of the Victorian era.
Queen Elizabeth I was on the throne in Britain.

exitQuiz.stem: In the unit 'Myths, legends and stories that inspire', one of the myths is called 'The Fall of Icarus'. Match the most important characters from this myth to what we know about them.
exitQuiz.hint: Consider that in the myth, the character of Daedalus creates a set of wings for humans.
exitQuiz.feedback: Like many mythologies, the Greek myths include supernatural events, and tragic events. Here, a father sees his son drown.

match.left: a renowned inventor
a boy who drowns
a king who imprisons two of his subjects
a man who escapes a labyrinth created by Daedalus

exitQuiz.stem: Starting with the first, put these plot points from the myth 'the Fall of Icarus' ('Myths, legends and stories that inspire') in chronological order.
exitQuiz.hint: Start at the beginning. Why does Daedalus have to create wings for himself and his son?
exitQuiz.feedback: In many ways, this is a story of human inventiveness and intelligence – humans fly over the sea, like birds or gods. But it is also a story of excessive pride and ambition – Icarus believes he is invincible and ignores his father's advice.

order.text: King Minos imprisons Daedalus and Icarus.
Daedalus creates wings from wax and feathers so they can fly away.
Daedalus tells his son not to fly too close to the sun.
Icarus flies higher and higher, enjoying the feeling of flying.
The wax begins to melt as Icarus flies close to the sun.
Icarus falls into the sea and drowns.
Daedalus offers his wings to the god, Apollo, and swears never to fly again.

exitQuiz.stem: In 'Myths, legends and stories that inspire', we read the myth called 'The Fall of Icarus'. This myth is designed to teach us about the dangers of hubris. What does it mean to be full of hubris?
exitQuiz.hint: Consider that when Icarus shows off and flies higher and higher, we could describe him as being full of hubris.
exitQuiz.feedback: Icarus flies high in the sky, using the wings his father created. He feels like a god as he flies, and he feels invincible. Thus, he flies higher and higher until the sun melts the wax holding his wings together. His hubris leads to his early death.

exitQuiz.stem: In 'Myths, legends and stories that inspire', we look at a painting called 'Landscape with the Fall of Icarus'. The most important figures are shepherds and workers. What word best describes them?
exitQuiz.hint: Consider that to be hubristic means to be filled with pride.
exitQuiz.feedback: Surprisingly, one of the most famous paintings inspired by the myth focuses on labourers, not main characters. These humble figures who focus on their work and don't overreach are Icarus's opposite.

exitQuiz.stem: Found in many cultures, {{ }} are stories which explain how the world began and what the world is like and why.
exitQuiz.hint: Consider that the story of the Fall of Icarus is an example of this type of text.
exitQuiz.feedback: Many different cultures have their own myths and mythologies. The myths differ widely, but share some common features. For example, explaining how the world began, or certain social customs. They often involve supernatural characters or events.

exitQuiz.stem: In 'Myths, legends and stories that inspire', we look at a painting entitled '{{ }} with the Fall of Icarus', a painting inspired by a Greek myth.
exitQuiz.hint: Consider this word means all the visible features of an area of land.
exitQuiz.feedback: This word comes first in the title, showing the landscape (and the people in it) are more important than Icarus himself. In this way, the humble figures and the natural world are more important than the hubristic character of Icarus.

lessons.title: Exploring William Carlos Williams’s poem ‘Landscape with the fall of Icarus’
lessons.outcome: I can write an ekphrastic poem inspired by Bruegel's 'Landscape with the Fall of Icarus' and William Carlos Williams's poem of the same name.
keyLearningPoints: William Carlos Williams's 'Landscape with the Fall of Icarus' is an ekphrastic poem.
An ekphrastic poem is a poem which describes a piece of art, and is inspired by it.
Each of Williams’s seven stanzas refers to something in Pieter Bruegel's painting 'Landscape with the Fall of Icarus'.
Like Bruegel, Williams focuses on the natural world rather than Icarus himself.
Each line of Williams’s poem is enjambed - there is no punctuation at the end of any of the lines.

keywords.definition: stories which explain how the world began and what the world is like and why
a poem which describes a piece of art, and is inspired by it
when there is no punctuation at the end of a line of poetry
unimportant
the speed of something

equipment: Pupils need a copy of the poem 'Landscape with the Fall of Icarus' by William Carlos Williams from the 1991 Collected Poems: 1939-1962, Volume II published by New Directions.

starterQuiz.stem: In the unit 'Myths, legends and stories that inspire', we look at a painting called 'Landscape with the Fall of Icarus' by Pieter Bruegel. What type of story was this inspired by?
starterQuiz.hint: Consider that stories sometimes have morals. 'Morals' are not a genre.
starterQuiz.feedback: Many different cultures have their own myths and mythologies. The myths differ widely, but share some common features. For example, explaining how the world began, or certain social customs. They often involve supernatural characters or events.

starterQuiz.stem: Starting with the first, put these plot points from the myth 'The Fall of Icarus' ('Myths, legends and stories that inspire') in chronological order.
starterQuiz.hint: Start at the end. How does Daedalus show humility and grief at the end of the myth?
starterQuiz.feedback: This myth has inspired many artworks and poems. There is something in the story of Icarus's hubris, as well as the relationship between father and son, which ignites the imagination of creative people.

order.text: Daedalus and Icarus have been imprisoned by King Minos.
Daedalus creates wings from wax and feathers so they can fly away.
Daedalus tells his son not to fly too close to the sun.
Icarus flies higher and higher, enjoying the feeling of flying.
The wax begins to melt as Icarus flies close to the sun.
Icarus falls into the sea and drowns.
Daedalus offers his wings to the god, Apollo, and swears never to fly again.

starterQuiz.stem: In the unit 'Myths, legends and stories that inspire', we look at a painting called 'Landscape with the Fall of Icarus' by Pieter Bruegel. Who is the smallest figure (person) in this painting?
starterQuiz.hint: Consider that King Minos is not in Bruegel's landscape.
starterQuiz.feedback: Looking at the painting for the first time, you could be forgiven for not noticing Icarus at all. He is given a small space at the bottom right hand side of the canvas, and we can only see his legs. It is our job to evaluate why Bruegel did this.

starterQuiz.stem: In the unit 'Myths, legends and stories that inspire', we look at a painting called 'Landscape with the Fall of Icarus' by Pieter Bruegel. Who is the largest figure (person) in this painting?
starterQuiz.hint: Consider that King Minos is not in Bruegel's landscape.
starterQuiz.feedback: The farmer with the plough is the largest and most central figure in this painting. We are drawn to a man with a humble occupation, engaging with the natural landscape. Perhaps this is meant to be an additional comment on the hubris of Icarus.

starterQuiz.stem: In the unit 'Myths, legends and stories that inspire', we look at a painting called 'Landscape with the Fall of Icarus' by Pieter Bruegel. Which of these people or things are captured in the picture?
starterQuiz.hint: Consider that we see only Icarus's legs in the painting.
starterQuiz.feedback: Bruegel gives most of his attention to the natural landscape and items which help the humble agricultural workers do their jobs. His focus is not on humans flying nor on Daedalus's invention.

options.text: the wings made of wax and feathers

starterQuiz.stem: In the unit 'Myths and Legends', we look at a painting called 'Landscape with the Fall of Icarus' by Pieter Bruegel. Which of these people or things are not captured in the picture?
starterQuiz.hint: Consider that that the central figure is a farmer completing manual labour.
starterQuiz.feedback: Bruegel's 'Landscape with the Fall of Icarus' is just that – mainly landscape, with Icarus, his father and their tragedy captured in a small moment in the bottom right hand corner of the canvas.

options.text: the wings made of wax and feathers

exitQuiz.stem: In the unit 'Myths, legends and stories that inspire', we look at three pieces of art about the same set of characters: Daedalus and Icarus. Starting with the first, put them in chronological order.
exitQuiz.hint: Consider that Bruegel was painting in the 16th century.
exitQuiz.feedback: These 3 pieces of art all focus on the same 2 characters, but are expressed in different ways: a myth is usually told verbally, a painting is a piece of visual art and a poem is a text. Each adds layers of meaning and interpretation to one other.

order.text: the Greek myth of the fall of Icarus
Pieter Bruegel's painting 'Landscape with the Fall of Icarus'
William Carlos Williams’s poem 'Landscape with the Fall of Icarus'

exitQuiz.stem: A pupil argued, 'Pieter Bruegel's painting and William Carlos Williams's poem present Icarus’s death as trivial.' ('Myths, legends and stories that inspire') What does trivial mean?
exitQuiz.hint: Consider that to be full of hubris means to be excessively proud.
exitQuiz.feedback: Arguably, Bruegel presents Icarus's death as trivial by having the figures in his painting not notice his drowning. Williams, using Bruegel's painting as inspiration, mimics this, leaving Icarus's death to the last stanza of his poem.

exitQuiz.stem: In Williams's poem 'Landscape with the Fall of Icarus' ('Myths, legends and stories that inspire'), the poet uses no {{ }} throughout. This increases the pace we have to read the poem.
exitQuiz.hint: Consider this word means the marks we use to divide sentences and clauses within sentences.
exitQuiz.feedback: Williams made a conscious choice to use no punctuation, and it is up to us, as students of English, to consider why. Possibly, the speed with which we have to read the poem mimics the speed with which Icarus plunges into the sea.

exitQuiz.stem: In Williams's poem 'Landscape with the Fall of Icarus' ('Myths, legends and stories that inspire'), there is no punctuation at the end of any of the lines. What is this technique called?
exitQuiz.hint: Consider that alliteration is when you start two or more words with the same letter for effect.
exitQuiz.feedback: Each line of Williams's poem is enjambed. This dramatically increases the pace with which we have to read the poem, perhaps reflecting the speed with which Icarus plunges into the sea, or perhaps that life will continue despite his death.

exitQuiz.stem: Match the first six stanzas of Williams's poem 'Landscape with the Fall of Icarus' ('Myths, legends and stories that inspire') to its focus.
exitQuiz.hint: Consider that Williams starts big, locating us in spring before moving into smaller details.
exitQuiz.feedback: The poem, like the painting it is describing, focuses on the natural world, the season and the lively movement of the agricultural workers. Icarus seems almost an afterthought, a small and trivial splash in Stanza 7.

match.left: the season
a farmer
the lively natural world
the sea
the sun
the coast

exitQuiz.stem: Williams's poem 'Landscape with the Fall of Icarus' ('Myths, legends and stories that inspire') is an {{ }} poem, which means a poem which describes a piece of art, and is inspired by it.
exitQuiz.hint: Consider that this word comes from the Greek phrásis meaning 'speak out'.
exitQuiz.feedback: In his poem, Williams is both inspired by, but also describes, Bruegel's painting. In this way, the poem becomes a comment on the painting, adding layers of meaning.

lessons.title: Exploring W.H. Auden's poem 'Musée des Beaux Arts'
lessons.outcome: I can write a creative paragraph inspired by W.H. Auden’s ekphrastic poem 'Musée des Beaux Arts'.
keyLearningPoints: W.H. Auden’s poem ‘Musée des Beaux Arts’ is an ekphrastic poem.
An ekphrastic poem is a poem which describes a piece of art, and is inspired by it.
Each painting which inspired Auden’s ekphrastic poem depicts tragic events.
However, what inspired Auden were the people in the paintings who seem to have apathetic responses to the tragic events.
Auden focuses particularly on the apathy of the ploughman in Bruegel’s painting ‘Landscape with the Fall of Icarus’.

keywords.definition: a large piece of farming equipment that is used to plant seeds and turn over soil
a poem which describes a piece of art, and is inspired by it
showing little interest or feeling in response to something
any person who is regarded as a skilled painter who worked in Europe before 1800
death or suffering of someone because of their religious beliefs

equipment: You need a copy of the poem W.H. Auden's 'Musée des Beaux Arts' from the Curtis Brown  1979 edition of Selected Poems, edited by Edward Mendelson.

contentGuidance.description: Depiction of scary, confusing or unsettling events or characters placed in danger, including creation of a scary atmosphere through the use of music and sound.

starterQuiz.stem: Match each sentence stem to its ending, showing your knowledge of 'The Fall of Icarus' ('Myths, legends and stories that inspire').
starterQuiz.hint: Start at the beginning. Why does Daedalus have to construct the wings in the first place?
starterQuiz.feedback: This myth has been the source of inspiration for artists of all types over the centuries. The story of hubris and humility, father and son, is inspiring, as well as the idea of human suffering.

match.left: Daedalus and Icarus.
constructs wings so they can escape.
his son not to fly too close to the sun.
flies too close to the sun.
the god Apollo his wings, saying he will never fly again.

starterQuiz.stem: In the unit 'Myths, legends and stories that inspire', we look at a painting called 'Landscape with the Fall of Icarus' by Pieter Bruegel. What was Bruegel's painting inspired by?
starterQuiz.hint: Consider that the painting features Icarus and a supernatural event.
starterQuiz.feedback: Many different cultures have myths and mythologies. A myth from Greece inspired Bruegel for this particular painting. Myths are stories which explain how the world began, what it is like and sometimes, like this one, they contain a moral.

starterQuiz.stem: In the unit 'Myths, legends and stories that inspire', we look at a painting called 'Landscape with the Fall of Icarus' by Pieter Bruegel. How might we describe Icarus's death?
starterQuiz.hint: Consider that myths are examples of fiction.
starterQuiz.feedback: The death of Icarus is a human tragedy. Icarus, mortal, plunges into the sea and drowns, seemingly punished his hubris. This leaves Daedalus, his father, who both mourns for his son, and perhaps feels at fault.

starterQuiz.stem: In the unit 'Myths, legends and stories that inspire', we look at a painting called 'Landscape with the Fall of Icarus' by Pieter Bruegel. What do we see if Icarus in this painting?
starterQuiz.hint: Consider we see a small part of Icarus's body.
starterQuiz.feedback: Bruegel gives most of his attention to the natural landscape and items which help the humble agricultural workers do their jobs. His focus is not on humans flying nor on Daedalus's invention.

starterQuiz.stem: In the unit 'Myths and Legends', we look at a painting called 'Landscape with the Fall of Icarus' by Pieter Bruegel. Focus on the figures apart from Icarus. What words most accurately describe them?
starterQuiz.hint: Consider that to be distressed means to be suffering from anxiety, stress or unhappiness. How are the figures responding to Icarus's' fall?
starterQuiz.feedback: Bruegel portrays a calm landscape, with workers who are getting on with tasks and seemingly ignoring, or unaware, of Icarus. Bruegel may be celebrating their humble characters.

starterQuiz.stem: In the unit 'Myths, legends and stories that inspire', we look at an ekphrastic poem by Williams Carlos Williams. What is an ekphrastic poem?
starterQuiz.hint: Consider that a poem that uses alliteration throughout is called alliterative.
starterQuiz.feedback: Williams's poem is inspired by Bruegel's 'Landscape with the Fall of Icarus', and it is also describes it over the course of seven stanzas. The clear and powerful imagery, and the minimal focus on Icarus adds layers of meaning to the painting.

options.text: a poem that uses alliteration throughout
a poem inspired by an artwork

exitQuiz.stem: In the unit 'Myths, legends and stories that inspire', we look at four pieces of art about the same set of characters: Daedalus and Icarus. Starting with the first, put them in chronological order.
exitQuiz.hint: Consider that Auden's poem was written in 1938, and first published in 1940.
exitQuiz.feedback: These 4 pieces of art all focus on the same 2 characters, but are expressed in very different ways. Even the 2 poems approach the work differently, with Williams focusing more on the canvas itself, and Auden thinking more about the idea of suffering.

order.text: the Greek myth of the fall of Icarus
Pieter Breugel's painting 'Landscape with the Fall of Icarus'
W.H. Auden’s poem 'Musée des Beaux Arts'
William Carlos Williams’s poem 'Landscape with the Fall of Icarus'

exitQuiz.stem: In 'Myths, legends and stories that inspire', we focus on a poem by W.H. Auden called 'Musée des Beaux Arts'. What feeling does Auden explore in this poem?
exitQuiz.hint: Consider that to be full of hubris means to be excessively proud.
exitQuiz.feedback: Auden's poem is inspired by a number of paintings he saw in a museum in Belgium. He believed these paintings were particularly good at capturing apathetic figures who were not interested in human suffering.

exitQuiz.stem: In 'Myths, legends and stories that inspire', W.H. Auden's poem 'Musée des Beaux Arts' is an ekphrastic poem because …?
exitQuiz.hint: Consider that the word ekphrastic is about the content of the poem, not its form.
exitQuiz.feedback: Auden's poem was inspired after a trip to a museum in Belgium in which he saw a number of art works. Bruegel's 'Landscape with the Fall of Icarus' is explicitly mentioned, but two others are also described.

options.text: It is divided into just two stanzas.
It describes the art it is inspired by.

exitQuiz.stem: In W.H. Auden’s poem 'Musée des Beaux Arts' ('Myths, legends and stories that inspire'), who does Auden present as apathetic to the death of Icarus?
exitQuiz.hint: Consider that Daedalus is not mentioned in the poem.
exitQuiz.feedback: Auden focuses on the largest figure in Bruegel's painting: the ploughman. He considers how he might have heard the splash, but Icarus's death was not important to him, not even important enough to turn properly and see what the splash was.

exitQuiz.stem: In W.H. Auden's poem 'Musée des Beaux Arts' ('Myths, legends and stories that inspire'), Auden explores the idea of apathy. Which sentence uses the word apathy correctly?
exitQuiz.hint: To be apathetic means to show little interest or feeling in response to something.
exitQuiz.feedback: The idea of apathy is the central focus of Auden's poem. He presents intense suffering side by side with people who are eating, walking, skating or just getting on with a boring task.

options.text: The play was apathetic so no-one liked it.
The audience apathetically applauded and demanded more.
The play was shocking and everyone was upset and apathetic.
The play failed to shock; instead, the audience was apathetic.

exitQuiz.stem: Which sentence is best inspired by Auden's interpretation of Pieter Bruegel's ploughman in 'Landscape with the Fall of Icarus'? ('Myths, legends and stories that inspire').
exitQuiz.hint: Consider that the ploughman and shepherd are not concerned with Icarus, either in the painting nor the poem.
exitQuiz.feedback: Just as Auden was inspired by the painting to write, so too can we be inspired by it, and the poem which follows. In this way, we can become part of the story of the myth of Daedalus and Icarus.

options.text: Working together, the shepherd and ploughman pulled Icarus to safety.
The ploughman worked back and forth methodically through the field.
Since then, the ploughman knew, without doubt, he should have done something.
The ploughman saw the wings and feet, but he was glad Icarus was in the water.

lessons.title: Exploring William Carlos Williams's poem 'The Hunters in the Snow'
lessons.outcome: I can write an ekphrastic poem inspired by Bruegel's 'The Hunters in the Snow' and William Carlos Williams's poem of the same name.
keyLearningPoints: William Carlos Williams's 'The Hunters in the Snow' is an ekphrastic poem.
An ekphrastic poem is a poem which describes a piece of art, and is inspired by it.
Each of Williams's seven stanzas refers to something in Pieter Bruegel’s painting 'The Hunters in the Snow'.
Bruegel's 'The Hunters in the Snow' depicts a rural scene in winter.

keywords.definition: to portray in a picture or to describe in writing.
a poem which describes a piece of art, and is inspired by it.
depressed, downcast.
the countryside.

equipment: You need a copy of the poem 'The Hunters in the Snow' by William Carlos Williams from the 1991 Collected Poems: 1939-1962, Volume II published by New Directions.

contentGuidance.label: Depiction or discussion of violence or suffering
contentGuidance.description: Depiction or discussion of violence or fighting, including threats of violence or the aftermath of violence.

contentGuidance.label: Depiction or discussion of violence or suffering
contentGuidance.description: Animal cruelty.

starterQuiz.stem: In the unit 'Myths, legends and stories that inspire', we learn about a number of different artists and poets. Match each person to something we know about them.
starterQuiz.hint: Consider that Williams was inspired by Bruegel to write 'Landscape with the Fall of Icarus'.
starterQuiz.feedback: These people are all great artists in their own right but some of their most famous pieces of work 'speak' and connect to each other. Bruegel's painting of Icarus, for example, inspired both Williams and Auden to write poetry about it.

match.left: 16th century painter
20th century American poet
20th century British poet

starterQuiz.stem: In the unit 'Myths, legends and stories that inspire', we look at some poems by Williams Carlos Williams. Williams carefully selects the adjectives in his poems. Which of the following are adjectives?
starterQuiz.hint: Consider that an adjective is a describing word.
starterQuiz.feedback: The poems we look at describe paintings that Williams has been inspired by. When Williams selects adjectives, he adds layers of meaning to the painting because he is inferring things, or suggesting things, about the objects and figures he sees.

starterQuiz.stem: In the unit 'Myths, legends and stories that inspire', we look at some poems by Williams Carlos Williams. He uses a simile in one of them. What is a simile?
starterQuiz.hint: Consider that alliteration is when one or more words begin with the same letter.
starterQuiz.feedback: In many ways, Williams's poems can feel like simple descriptions of the paintings he is inspired by. But his careful choice of descriptive language, and his occasional use of simile are powerful moments, rich for analysis.

options.text: when one or more words begin with the same letter
repeating a word or phrase at the beginning of sentences
when you don't use any punctuation in a line of poetry
a method of comparison using 'like' or 'as'

starterQuiz.stem: In the unit 'Myths and Legends', we look at a poem called 'Landscape with the Fall of Icarus' by Williams Carlos Williams. Williams doesn't use any punctuation in this poem which increases the …?
starterQuiz.hint: Consider that rhyme is when two or more words have a similar sound.
starterQuiz.feedback: Just as a poet pays close attention to the words in their work, so too do they make careful choices about punctuation. We can analyse these choices in the same way as we analyse their word choice.

starterQuiz.stem: In the unit 'Myths, legends and stories that inspire', we look at a poem called 'Landscape with the Fall of Icarus' by Williams Carlos Williams. What type of poem is it?
starterQuiz.hint: Consider that Williams's poem is inspired by a painting and describes it.
starterQuiz.feedback: Ekphrastic poems are both inspired by paintings, but also describe them in the poems themselves. This technique adds layers of meaning to a painting. You could try to write some ekphrastic poetry the next time you see a painting you like!

starterQuiz.stem: In the unit 'Myths, legends and stories that inspire', we look at some poems by Williams Carlos Williams. Williams uses enjambment in every line of these poems. What does this mean?
starterQuiz.hint: Consider that enjambment means 'running on' and speeds up the pace of a poem.
starterQuiz.feedback: Just as a writer chooses what words and language techniques they want to use, so too do they select how they will use punctuation. In the poems we look at, Williams uses enjambment in every line, perhaps mimicking how the eye travels over a painting.

options.text: each line of poetry ends in a full stop
his poem is inspired by a piece of art
his poem describes a piece of art
his poem doesn't use any punctuation
his poem has the same title as the painting it describes

exitQuiz.stem: Williams Carlos Williams poem 'The Hunters in the Snow' (Myths, legends and stories that inspire) is an ekphrastic poem. Why is it an ekphrastic poem?
exitQuiz.hint: Consider that poems that are not ekphrastic can include enjambment.

starterQuiz.stem: In the unit 'Myths, Legends and stories', we look at two paintings by Pieter Bruegel. What are their names?
starterQuiz.hint: Consider that an Old Master is a term for any person who is regarded as a skilled painter who worked in Europe before 1800.
starterQuiz.feedback: Bruegel is considered one of the Old Masters. His skill as a painter is renowned, not only for his paintings themselves, but the other artworks that his paintings inspire. Auden's 'Musée des Beaux Arts' is just one example.

starterQuiz.stem: In the unit 'Myths, Legends and stories that inspire', we look at a painting called 'The Hunters in the Snow' by Pieter Bruegel. What is in the background of this painting?
starterQuiz.hint: Consider that background means the surroundings that appear furthest away from the viewer.
starterQuiz.feedback: The painting captures a landscape during winter. The mountains and sky serve as the backdrop for the smaller figures and natural features in the foreground.

starterQuiz.stem: In the unit 'Myths, Legends and stories that inspire', we look at a painting called 'The Hunters in the Snow' by Pieter Bruegel. What is in the foreground of this painting?
starterQuiz.hint: Consider that foreground means part of the view that is closest to the viewer.
starterQuiz.feedback: The painting captures a landscape during winter. The hunters are bottom left, the largest figures in the painting, hence the painting's name. The bush in the foreground is specifically mentioned in William Carlos Williams's poem inspired by Bruegel.

starterQuiz.stem: In the unit 'Myths, Legends and stories that inspire', we look at a painting called 'The Hunters in the Snow' by Pieter Bruegel. What is true of this painting?
starterQuiz.hint: Consider that Bruegel never painted any portraits, which are pictures of people, usually depicting their head and shoulders. Bruegel is famous, instead, for his paintings of landscapes.
starterQuiz.feedback: This painting has inspired poems of lots of different names, all connected to the season of winter. This landscape seems to capture much of what the season is like: the beauty of the snow, but also its harshness.

The final sentence of a comparative paragraph could link to the topic sentence.

exitQuiz.stem: When writing about the texts we explore in 'Myths, legends and stories that inspire', you will start analytical paragraphs with topic sentences. What is true of topic sentences?
exitQuiz.hint: Consider that topic sentences shouldn't have multiple focuses.
exitQuiz.feedback: Developing your ability to write clear topic sentences takes time. A powerful topic sentence gives your essay and its ideas structure, and sets you up for success for the paragraph.

options.text: They explain whether you like the text or not.

exitQuiz.hint: Consider that analytical topic sentences shouldn't involve personal pronouns.

exitQuiz.feedback: De la Mare draws attention to the purpose of the spears – which is to kill animals. These objects, and the hunters themselves, perhaps contrast to the skaters who are described as having fun on the ice.

exitQuiz.stem: Starting with the first sentence, order this comparative paragraph about two poems from 'Myths, legends and stories that inspire'.
exitQuiz.hint: Consider that the first sentence of a comparative paragraph should be a topic sentence that states what the paragraph will be about.
exitQuiz.feedback: A comparative paragraph requires us to analyse 2 texts, which can sometimes feel challenging. A helpful structure can be to start with a  topic sentence followed by analysis/comparison of quotations and a concluding sentence summing up your ideas.

order.text: Both de la Mare and Williams convey how treacherous the winter mountains can be.

keyLearningPoints: The Lady of Shalott is a cursed woman who is confined to a tower on an island just outside Camelot.
The Lady of Shalott isn't allowed to look out of the tower's window, but sees the outside through a mirror's reflection.
The Lady of Shalott must weave these reflections into a cloth; if she stops weaving, something terrible will happen.
One day she looks out of the window in order to see Sir Lancelot.
The curse comes upon her and she dies, found in a boat drifting toward Camelot.

starterQuiz.stem: In 'Myths, Legends and stories that inspire’, we will read a poem written by Alfred, Lord Tennyson who was born in 1809 and died in 1892. Who was the British monarch for most of Tennyson's adult life?

starterQuiz.feedback: Alfred, Lord Tennyson was a Victorian. This means he was writing when Queen Victoria was on the throne. Indeed, he was the Poet Laureate during much of this time, a position given by the monarch as a reward for writing brilliant poetry.

starterQuiz.stem: In 'Myths, Legends and stories that inspire’, we will read a poem written by Alfred, Lord Tennyson who was an important poet in the Victorian era. When was the Victorian era?
starterQuiz.hint: Consider that 1939-1945 are the dates for World War Two, a time when King George VI was on the throne.
starterQuiz.feedback: Queen Victoria reigned for 63 years. Alfred, Lord Tennyson was Poet Laureate for much of this time (1850-92). Being Poet Laureate is an honour given by the monarch for being a brilliant poet. The position still exists today.

lessons.title: Symbolism in Alfred, Lord Tennyson's ‘The Lady of Shalott’
lessons.outcome: I can explore Tennyson's use of symbolism in 'The Lady of Shallot'.
keyLearningPoints: Symbolism is when writers use something tangible to represent an intangible idea.
The Lady of Shalott symbolises the isolated artist and the sacrifices some make to create great art.
Throughout the poem, Tennyson emphasises that the Lady of Shalott is a great artist.
However, Tennyson also emphasises how much the Lady of Shalott sacrifices to create her beautiful art.
It is up to the reader to decide whether the Lady of Shalott made the right decision to leave her isolated tower.

lessons.title: Descriptive writing using Lord Tennyson's 'The Lady of Shalott' as stimulus
lessons.outcome: I can create a powerful atmosphere in my creative writing through language choices and symbolism inspired by Alfred, Lord Tennyson’s ‘The Lady of Shalott’.
keyLearningPoints: Symbolism is when writers use something tangible to represent an intangible idea.
Tennyson’s use of symbols is one way he creates a sombre atmosphere, particularly in Part 4 of ‘The Lady of Shalott’.
Key symbols in ‘The Lady of Shalott’ include a willow tree to symbolise grief, and a pearl to symbolise perfection.
Tennyson also relies on pathetic fallacy to create a sombre and dramatic atmosphere in Part 4 of the poem.
You can employ pathetic fallacy and symbolism in your own writing to create a distinctive atmosphere.

lessons.title: Effective sensory language using ‘The Execution of Lady Jane Grey’ as stimulus
lessons.outcome: I can employ the five senses in my descriptive writing to create a chosen effect.
keyLearningPoints: Sensory language is writing that includes reference to some, or all, of the five senses.
You don't need to write, 'They could see, feel, taste, touch, hear ...' when using sensory language.
Instead, you can evoke the senses by starting with the noun you wish to describe.
Adjectives should be chosen carefully so that they create particular effects.

keywords.definition: writing that includes reference to some, or all, of the five senses

of an emotion, to keep it hidden or bottled up

starterQuiz.stem: Identify the adjective in the following sentence: 'The pale straw was strewn on the floor carelessly.' ('Myths, Legends and stories that inspire').
starterQuiz.hint: Consider that the word 'carelessly' is used to describe the verb. This makes it an adverb.
starterQuiz.feedback: Adjectives describe nouns, and can create atmosphere in a piece of descriptive writing. You should be experimental, imaginative and daring with your adjectives in some of your writing so you can explore their different effects!

starterQuiz.stem: Identify the noun in the following sentence: 'The velvet cushion was green, bordered with gold.' ('Myths, Legends and stories that inspire').
starterQuiz.hint: Consider which words describe, and which word name something.
starterQuiz.feedback: Nouns are naming words. Often, in descriptive writing, there will be a particular item we want to describe in detail. It might be the focus of one or more sentences, or even a whole paragraph.

starterQuiz.stem: Identify the verb in the following sentence: 'Her trembling hand reached out into the air.' ('Myths, Legends and stories that inspire').
starterQuiz.hint: Consider that the word 'trembling' is used here to describe the hand, making it an adjective.
starterQuiz.feedback: Verbs are doing or being words. We have so many different and wonderful verbs in English to convey exactly how a particular action is done. As such, when you are choosing your verbs for your creative writing, you should be experimental and ambitious.

Strategies like reading aloud, reading backwards or reading with a particular focus can help you proofread successfully.

units.title: 'A Midsummer Night's Dream'
units.description: In this unit, pupils read and explore Shakespeare's comedy 'A Midsummer Night's Dream'. They focus on the character Puck and the theme of the supernatural, and analyse their role and importance at different points in the play. Finally, they plan and write an essay about Puck and the supernatural.

lessons.outcome: I can explain the plot and main themes of Shakespeare’s ‘A Midsummer Night’s Dream’.
keyLearningPoints: ‘A Midsummer Night’s Dream’ is a Shakespearean comedy.
There are three sets of characters in the play.
The play starts and ends in Athens; in the middle, the play is set in a magical forest.
The play ends with a number of marriages.
A summary of the plot helps us understand some of the play’s main themes.

starterQuiz.stem: What type of texts did William Shakespeare write?
starterQuiz.hint: Consider that although many of Shakespeare's texts explore religious themes and ideas, he did not write sermons to be delivered in church.
starterQuiz.feedback: Shakespeare wrote 39 plays, 154 sonnets (14 line poems) and three narrative poems (poems which tell a story).

starterQuiz.stem: Whilst books are usually divided into chapters, what are plays divided into?
starterQuiz.hint: Consider that poems are divided into stanzas (verses).
starterQuiz.feedback: All of Shakespeare's plays are divided into acts. These acts are divided into scenes. A change of act or scene can signal a change in location, mood or time.

starterQuiz.stem: All of Shakespeare's plays are divided into acts. How many acts is each divided into?
starterQuiz.hint: Consider that there is an act for the climax of the play, and an act for the resolution of the play. How many additional acts might be needed to establish characters, and to allow the plot to develop?
starterQuiz.feedback: The five acts usually follow this structure: exposition (establishing characters), rising action, climax, falling action, resolution.

starterQuiz.stem: Shakespeare wrote a number of comedies. Which of the following of Shakespeare's plays are comedies?
starterQuiz.hint: Consider that 'Romeo and Juliet' ends in the death, rather than marriage, of a young hero and heroine.
starterQuiz.feedback: Shakespeare's plays are (roughly) divided into comedies, tragedies and histories. Some people define some of his plays as 'problem plays' because they contain both comedy and tragedy.

starterQuiz.stem: 'A Midsummer Night's Dream' is a Shakespearean comedy. What common features do Shakespearean comedies share?
starterQuiz.hint: Consider that 'A Midsummer Night's Dream' has a number of songs in it.
starterQuiz.feedback: Whilst sad or cruel things can happen in Shakespeare's comedies, there is a light-hearted tone, laughter and merriment throughout.

options.text: often include the death of the villain

starterQuiz.stem: The title of 'A Midsummer Night's Dream' could tell us something about what to expect in the play. What inferences could we make about this title?
starterQuiz.hint: Consider that the theatre can transport you to many places - real and imaginary - so having a play about a midsummer's dream could be set in winter and it wouldn't matter.
starterQuiz.feedback: Looking at any text's title is always a useful way in to starting to understand it, and what the writer might want us to take away from their work.

options.text: The characters in the play will all be asleep

exitQuiz.stem: 'A Midsummer Night's Dream' is set in two different places. What are the two settings?
exitQuiz.hint: Consider that Shakespeare was born in England, but the play is set elsewhere.
exitQuiz.feedback: The first and last acts of the play take place in Athens. Acts 2, 3 and 4 take place in the magical forest.

exitQuiz.stem: In 'A Midsummer Night's Dream', who does Egeus want his daughter, Hermia, to marry?
exitQuiz.hint: Consider that, in the world of the play, Egeus doesn't know that Oberon, King of the Fairies, exists.
exitQuiz.feedback: The play opens with Egeus furious with his daughter, Hermia, who wants to marry Lysander. This is not the man Egeus has picked for his daughter and he wants her to obey him, or be punished for her disobedience.

keyLearningPoints: The First Folio divides Shakespeare’s plays into tragedies, histories and comedies.
An additional genre - tragicomedies - has been used to describe plays which combine both tragic and comic elements.
Shakespearean comedies usually focus on love, and end in marriage.
The plots of comedies are often intricate and include a number of surprises and plot twists.
Shakespearean comedies often include slapstick humour.

starterQuiz.stem: How might we define Shakespeare's 'A Midsummer Night's Dream'?
starterQuiz.hint: Consider the overall tone and plot of the play. Are we meant to laugh, cry or learn from it?
starterQuiz.feedback: Understanding the play's genre means we can understand the types of things we might expect to see in the play. For example, the play ending in a number of marriages.

starterQuiz.stem: In 'A Midsummer Night's Dream', there are a number of sets of different characters. What sets of characters are there?
starterQuiz.hint: Consider that the actors are desperate to put on a play for the Athenian nobles so they can earn some much needed money.
starterQuiz.feedback: The different sets of characters are all distinct (different) but their storylines sometimes connect. For example, when Bottom, a poor Athenian actor, is in a potion-induced relationship with Titania, Queen of the Fairies.

starterQuiz.stem: In 'A Midsummer Night's Dream', there is much chaos and confusion. Which characters are the source of the chaos and confusion?
starterQuiz.hint: Consider that Egeus is very clear about what he wants his daughter Hermia to do: marry Demetrius.
starterQuiz.feedback: Puck carries out Oberon's wishes - to put the magical potion onto Titania and an Athenian man. However, Puck adds to the chaos and confusion by transforming Bottom's head into the head of a donkey, and putting the magical potion on the wrong man.

starterQuiz.stem: Which characters marry each other at the end of 'A Midsummer Night's Dream'?
starterQuiz.hint: Consider that at the end of the play, all four Athenian noble people get married and are happy with their given partner.
starterQuiz.feedback: At the end of the play Theseus allows Lysander and Hermia to marry, despite her father's anger. Demetrius, who is still under the spell of the magical potion, now loves Helena and is happy to marry her instead of Hermia.

starterQuiz.stem: In 'A Midsummer Night's Dream', which three characters have the magical love potion used on them?
starterQuiz.hint: Consider that Puck has control of the magical love potion. He puts it on people, rather than it being used on him.
starterQuiz.feedback: At the end of the play, the magical love potion is removed from Titania and Lysander. However, it remains on Demetrius and this is why he is happy to marry Helena.

starterQuiz.stem: Starting with the first plot point of 'A Midsummer Night's Dream', put the plot points relating to the Athenian noble people in order.
starterQuiz.hint: Start at the beginning. Why do Hermia and Lysander decide to run away from Athens?
starterQuiz.feedback: The plot of 'A Midsummer Night's Dream' is confusing - it is meant to be! Part of the fun of Shakespearean comedies are the plot twists and misunderstandings!

order.text: Egeus and Theseus threaten to punish Hermia if she doesn't marry Demetrius.
Lysander and Hermia decide to run away from Athens.
Demetrius and Helena follow Lysander and Hermia into the magical forest.
Puck puts the magical love potion on Lysander, who falls in love with Helena.
Puck puts the magical love potion on Demetrius, who falls in love with Helena.
Puck removes the magical love potion from Lysander; he loves Hermia again.
The four Athenian noble people return to Athens and get married.

exitQuiz.stem: The First Folio - the first collection of Shakespeare's plays published in 1623 - divides his plays into what categories?
exitQuiz.hint: Consider that the term tragicomedy was applied to some of Shakespeare's plays long after the First Folio was first published.
exitQuiz.feedback: Each of these genres has some key features which help us understand what we might expect to find in the play. For example, a tragedy includes the death of a great hero.

exitQuiz.stem: A pupil said: 'A Midsummer Night's Dream' is a tragedy." How would you correct them?
exitQuiz.hint: Consider that some quite terrible things do happen in the play, and a number of different characters are distressed or tricked at different points. But overall, the tone is comedic, and overall, we are meant to find the chaos and confusion funny.
exitQuiz.feedback: The play's supernatural fairies do provide a source of comedy, particularly the character of Puck, but many of Shakespeare's plays include the supernatural, and they are not all comedies.

options.text: The play is a comedy because it ends in a number of marriages.
The play is a comedy because nothing bad happens in it.
The play is a comedy because it includes the supernatural.
The play is a comedy because it involves misunderstandings.
The play is a comedy because some of it is set in a forest.

exitQuiz.stem: Shakespeare's plays are often defined by their genre. Match each genre to its key features.
exitQuiz.hint: Start with comedy. Consider the plot of 'A Midsummer Night's Dream' (a comedy) and then relook at the definitions.
exitQuiz.feedback: The First Folio (the first book of Shakespeare's plays) divided the plays into comedies, tragedies and histories. Later, scholars added the term tragicomedy to define some of the plays which don't seem to fit either the tragedy or comedy genre.

match.left: presents young people in love, and ends in marriage
explores complex emotions like jealousy or ambition; ends in death
about English history; explore what it means to be a good monarch
contain elements of comedy and tragedy

exitQuiz.stem: In order to discuss the genre of 'A Midsummer Night's Dream' accurately, you could use a number of key terms. Match the key terms to their definitions.
exitQuiz.hint: Consider this sentence which uses the word intricate correctly: "The plot of 'A Midsummer Night's Dream' can be really confusing. There are many characters and the plot is so intricate that I often lose track of who is in love with who!"
exitQuiz.feedback: Discussing the play's genre is a good way in to understanding the purpose of a play, and what you might expect to find in it. Using key terms will make sure your analysis is accurate and precise.

match.left: the style or type of text: for example science fiction
a play that makes you laugh, involving misunderstandings and marriage
complicated
physical comedy, sometimes violent but intended to make people laugh
the first collection of most of Shakespeare’s plays, published in 1623

exitQuiz.stem: The first published collection of Shakespeare's plays is called the {{ }}.
exitQuiz.hint: Consider this is a two word phrase. The first word means before all others.
exitQuiz.feedback: The First Folio is considered one of the most influential books of all times. Published in 1623, the plays it includes have impacted the world of English Literature, and so much more, for centuries.

exitQuiz.stem: In 'A Midsummer Night's Dream', Titania falls in love with Bottom, who has had his head transformed into that of a donkey. Why does this plot point reinforce the idea the play is a comedy?
exitQuiz.hint: Consider that many of Shakespeare's plays involve the supernatural, and they are not all comedies.
exitQuiz.feedback: Comedies often involve misunderstandings, as in the case of Bottom, and slapstick comedy. Whilst slapstick comedy can sometimes be violent and unsettling, its purpose is to entertain.

options.text: they end up getting married, which is how comedies end
it is a moment of slapstick comedy
Bottom doesn't know what has happened or why

lessons.outcome: I can explore how the patriarchy is presented in William Shakespeare’s ‘A Midsummer Night’s Dream’, focusing on the openings of Act 1 and Act 2.
keyLearningPoints: Athens is a patriarchal society.
Egeus has the right to kill his daughter.
Act 1 and Act 2 both begin with a conflict.
It could be argued that Titania is presented as Oberon's equal.
Oberon has to use a magical love potion on Titania in order to get what he wants.

words from a text

a serious argument

starterQuiz.stem: In 'A Midsummer Night's Dream', why is Egeus angry at the start of the play?
starterQuiz.hint: Consider that Theseus and Egeus are friends in Act 1.
starterQuiz.feedback: Egeus has planned for his daughter to marry Demetrius. She wants to marry Lysander. As such, he brings her before Theseus so that she can be punished for her disobedience.

options.text: Theseus won't let his daughter marry Demetrius
He can't find the magical love potion he needs
His daughter wants to marry Lysander
His daughter wants to marry Theseus
His daughter is in love with Demetrius

starterQuiz.stem: In 'A Midsummer Night's Dream', what does the magical love potion do?
starterQuiz.hint: Consider that although Titania does fall in love with someone who has the head of a donkey, that is coincidence rather than the nature of the love potion.
starterQuiz.feedback: The magical love potion is the cause of much chaos and confusion because it makes you fall in love with the first person you see after you wake up. Going to sleep, in 'A Midsummer Night's Dream', is a dangerous business!

options.text: makes you fall in love with your true love
makes you fall in love with yourself
makes you fall in love with an animal
makes you fall in love with the next person you see after you wake up
makes you fall out of love with your partner

starterQuiz.stem: In 'A Midsummer Night's Dream', who does Titania fall in love with when under the influence of the magical love potion?
starterQuiz.hint: Consider that Titania doesn't interact with the Athenian nobles.
starterQuiz.feedback: Puck puts the magical potion on Titania as she is sleeping. When she wakes up, she falls in love with one of the Athenian actors, Bottom. Puck makes this relationship even more ridiculous by transforming Bottom's head into that of a donkey.

starterQuiz.stem: In 'A Midsummer Night's Dream', there is lots of conflict throughout the play. Match the pairs of characters with their conflict.
starterQuiz.hint: Start with Act 1. Consider that the play begins in Athens, not the magical forest. Why is there conflict in Athens?
starterQuiz.feedback: There are many problems between fathers and daughters, and different partners. The magical love potion increases the conflict as it causes chaos and confusion. But at the end of the play, all of the conflicts are resolved.

match.left: argue about who Hermia should marry
argue about who gets to be in charge of a little boy
argue at the beginning of the play because one doesn't love the other
argue over which man loves them and why

starterQuiz.stem: Starting with the first plot point, track Titania's storyline in chronological order through the play, 'A Midsummer Night's Dream'.
starterQuiz.hint: Start at the beginning. What is the source of the conflict between Oberon and Titania?
starterQuiz.feedback: The end of Titania's story is interesting as she has been humiliated, by having fallen in love with Bottom, but also has lost the boy she wanted keep. She and Oberon are no longer in conflict, but it has come at some cost to Titania.

order.text: Titania refuses to give Oberon the little boy she looks after to be his servant.
Oberon plots revenge on Titania.
Oberon puts a magical love potion on Titania's eyes as she sleeps.
Titania wakes up and falls in love with Bottom, who has the head of a donkey.
Titania dotes on Bottom.
Oberon gets the little boy from Titania.
Oberon removes the magical love potion and he and Titania make up.

starterQuiz.stem: Starting with the first plot point, order the events of Act 1 of 'A Midsummer Night's Dream' in chronological order.
starterQuiz.hint: Start at the end. Consider how Shakespeare creates the plot so that all four Athenian noble people end up in the magical forest in Act 2.
starterQuiz.feedback: The first Act is set in Athens and we see a strict order and hierarchy to people's lives: Hermia must obey her father, Egeus must obey Theseus. We see this setting contrasted in Act 2, 3 and 4 where there is chaos and disorder in the magical forest.

order.text: Egeus complains to Theseus that his daughter wants to marry Lysander.
Egeus asks Theseus if he can kills his daughter if she doesn't obey him.
Theseus advises Hermia to marry Demetrius, or she will be killed.
Lysander and Hermia decide to run away from Athens.
Hermia and Lysander tell Helena that they are going to run away.
Helena decides to tell Demetrius about Hermia and Lysander's plan.
Helena decides to follow Demetrius as he pursues Hermia.

exitQuiz.stem: In Act 1 of 'A Midsummer Night's Dream', Hermia is told she will be punished if she doesn't obey her father. What punishments could she face?
exitQuiz.hint: Consider that Hermia wants to marry Lysander.
exitQuiz.feedback: Hermia's punishments are extreme: a forced marriage, imprisonment in a nunnery or death. Although the play is a comedy, it also contains some darker elements and ideas, which are clearly displayed in Act 1.

exitQuiz.stem: In what ways are the openings of Acts 1 and 2 of 'A Midsummer Night's Dream' similar?
exitQuiz.hint: Consider that two of the play's Acts are set in Athens. Which are they?
exitQuiz.feedback: In Act 1, we see a father-daughter conflict presented. In Act 2, we see a conflict between two partners. In both cases, men make demands and threats of the women they are supposed to love.

options.text: both see an angry father demand something of their daughter
both are set in the magical forest

exitQuiz.stem: In 'A Midsummer Night's Dream', how does Titania respond when Oberon asks her to give him the little boy she looks after?
exitQuiz.hint: Consider that Puck is Oberon's servant, not Titania's.
exitQuiz.feedback: When Oberon demands, "Give me that boy", Titania replies, "Not for thy fairy kingdom". It is only through trickery and magic that Oberon can get what he wants.

options.text: She says no and creates a plan to punish him for his request.
She says no and asks Puck to help protect her.
She says she will if he gives her his fairy kingdom.
She says yes, but only after he makes her fall in love with Bottom.
She says yes, but then wants the boy back when she falls in love with Bottom.

exitQuiz.stem: In 'A Midsummer Night's Dream', Athens is presented as a {{}} society, a society in which men hold the power and the laws and structure of the society prevent women from having power.
exitQuiz.hint: Consider this word comes from the Greek 'patriarkhes' meaning ruling father.
exitQuiz.feedback: Athens is presented as a patriarchal society. We see this through the presentation of Egeus who is able to control and punish his daughter as he sees fit because he is her father.

exitQuiz.stem: In Act 1 of 'A Midsummer Night's Dream', Theseus tells Hermia that "To you, your father should be as a..."
exitQuiz.hint: Consider this word means a very powerful being who deserves to be worshipped.
exitQuiz.feedback: This simile conveys the patriarchal society of Athens, one in which men are considered superior to women, and the expectation is that women obey men.

exitQuiz.stem: In Act 1 of 'A Midsummer Night's Dream', Egeus says of Hermia, "As she is {{}}, I may dispose of her".
exitQuiz.hint: Consider this word means Hermia belongs to Egeus.
exitQuiz.feedback: This phrase conveys the patriarchal society of Athens, a society in which women are considered the property of their father or husband.

lessons.title: The presentation of Egeus in Shakespeare's 'A Midsummer Night's Dream'
lessons.outcome: I can explain how Shakespeare presents the character of Egeus in ‘A Midsummer Night’s Dream’, including considering relevant context.
keyLearningPoints: ‘A Midsummer Night’s Dream’ was first performed to an Elizabethan audience.
Elizabethans believed women should obey their fathers and husbands.
Elizabethans believed the supernatural was evil.
Shakespeare included ideas about the patriarchy and the supernatural in his plays as a way to connect to his audiences.
When writing about ‘A Midsummer Night’s Dream’, you should include context to help develop your ideas.

starterQuiz.stem: In 'A Midsummer Night's Dream', what is the name of Hermia's father?
starterQuiz.hint: Consider that Lysander is the name of the man Hermia wishes to marry.
starterQuiz.feedback: The play begins with Egeus complaining about his daughter who wishes to marry Lysander. Egeus has not agreed to this marriage and feels Hermia should be punished for her disobedience.

starterQuiz.stem: Where is 'A Midsummer Night's Dream' set?
starterQuiz.hint: Consider that the play will be performed in a theatre, but a playwright can create any setting in this space. A play could be set at sea, or on the moon, for example.
starterQuiz.feedback: The first Act of the play is set in Athens. The play then moves to a magical forest just outside Athens for Acts 2, 3 and 4 before returning to the city in Act 5.

starterQuiz.stem: In 'A Midsummer Night's Dream', who does Egeus want Hermia to marry?
starterQuiz.hint: Consider that the character of Oberon is a magical fairy who lives in the forest. Egeus, who lives in Athens, doesn't know about Oberon.
starterQuiz.feedback: Egeus tells Theseus that Demetrius has his "consent" to marry Hermia, not Lysander.

starterQuiz.stem: In 'A Midsummer Night's Dream', Hermia faces punishment if she doesn't obey her father and marry Demetrius. What punishments does she face?
starterQuiz.hint: Consider that Hermia chooses to go into the forest, running away from Athens with Lysander so they can get married.
starterQuiz.feedback: Despite the play being a comedy, it does contain darker elements. The opening, with the very serious punishments that Hermia faces, is just one example.

options.text: banishment to the forest outside Athens
forced marriage to a man she doesn't love

starterQuiz.stem: In 'A Midsummer Night's Dream', what supernatural or magical elements does Shakespeare include in the play?
starterQuiz.hint: Consider that the magical potion is very important in the play, but what is its power?
starterQuiz.feedback: The play has magical characters, and supernatural happenings. The magical elements add comedy, although they could also be interpreted as scary and cruel. For example, Bottom's head being transformed into that of a donkey.

starterQuiz.stem: In 'A Midsummer Night's Dream', why might we describe Athens, where the play is set, as patriarchal?
starterQuiz.hint: Consider that word comes from the Greek patriarkhēs meaning 'the father or chief of the race'.
starterQuiz.feedback: Shakespeare begins the play with a scene that makes it clear Athens is patriarchal. Egeus, Hermia's father, is angry at his daughter for disobeying him, and he is allowed to punish her severely for this disobedience which he states is "due" to him.

options.text: It's a society in which women are considered equal to men.
It's a society in which women are considered superior to men.
It's a society in which women are considered inferior to men.
It's a society in which women are considered equal to fairies.
It's a society in which women are considered inferior to fairies.

exitQuiz.stem: 'A Midsummer Night's Dream' was first performed in around 1595. What is the name for the play's first audiences?
exitQuiz.hint: Consider that the characters in the play are called Athenians because the play is set in Athens.
exitQuiz.feedback: The monarch of England when Shakespeare wrote the play was Elizabeth I. As such, we call those who first watched the play Elizabethan.

exitQuiz.stem: Who was on the throne when Shakespeare wrote 'A Midsummer Night's Dream'?
exitQuiz.hint: Consider that Queen Elizabeth II died in 2022. The play was first written and performed in about 1595.
exitQuiz.feedback: The play's first audiences are called Elizabethan, after their monarch. Knowing about Elizabethan society and attitudes is an excellent way to understand some of the ideas that Shakespeare presents and explores in his play.

exitQuiz.stem: 'A Midsummer Night's Dream' was first watched by an Elizabethan audience. What were some common expectations of Elizabethan women?
exitQuiz.hint: Consider that Elizabethan society was patriarchal.
exitQuiz.feedback: The play's opening, which sees a daughter disobey her father, would have enraged an Elizabethan audience because of their strict ideas about the patriarchy.

options.text: to accept their superiority to men
to accept their inferiority to men

exitQuiz.stem: A pupil said, 'When 'A Midsummer Night's Dream' was first performed, women were considered men's equals.' How might you respond to this statement?
exitQuiz.hint: Consider that Elizabethans believed the supernatural was evil and connected to the devil.
exitQuiz.feedback: Elizabethan society was patriarchal, and so is the world of Athens where the play is set. Looking at the language Egeus uses in Act 1, Scene 1 can be a useful way to understand the rights and privileges men had over the women in their lives.

options.text: Correct - because when the play was written, the monarch was a woman.
Correct - this is why Hermia has the power to run away from Athens.
Incorrect - women were considered superior because the monarch was a woman.
Incorrect - women were considered equal only if they had supernatural powers.

exitQuiz.stem: In Act 1, Scene 1 of 'A Midsummer Night's Dream', Egeus says Lysander has "{{ }}" Hermia and that is why she has fallen in love with him.
exitQuiz.hint: Consider that this word means to put a spell on someone.
exitQuiz.feedback: This word suggests Egeus thinks of Lysander as evil and dangerous. It also shows that he believes Hermia wouldn't disobey him on purpose, and must have been tricked into wanting to marry Lysander rather than the man her father has selected.

exitQuiz.stem: In Act 1, Scene 1 of 'A Midsummer Night's Dream', Egeus says Demetrius has his "{{ }}" to marry Hermia, whereas Lysander does not.
exitQuiz.hint: Consider this word is a synonym for permission.
exitQuiz.feedback: This word shows how much control Egeus expects to have over his daughter. She is only allowed to do things that he gives permission for. As such, Egeus could be interpreted as a powerful patriarch.

starterQuiz.stem: In 'A Midsummer Night's Dream', who is Titania?
starterQuiz.hint: Consider that, like Lysander, Demetrius wants to marry Hermia at the start of the play.
starterQuiz.feedback: Titania has a high status, equal to that of Oberon. As such, her love for Bottom, a low status character with a donkey for a head, is meant to be a humiliating punishment from Oberon.

options.text: the woman Demetrius wants to marry

starterQuiz.stem: In 'A Midsummer Night's Dream', who is Oberon?
starterQuiz.hint: Consider that Oberon has a high status.
starterQuiz.feedback: Oberon, like Titania, rules over the magical forest. He and his servant, Puck, cause the chaos and confusion that occurs in Acts 2 and 3.

options.text: one of the poor Athenian actors
the man Egeus wants Hermia to marry

starterQuiz.stem: In 'A Midsummer Night's Dream', why are Titania and Oberon in conflict?
starterQuiz.hint: Consider that Titania never finds out that Oberon made her fall in love with Bottom.
starterQuiz.feedback: Just like Act 1, Act 2 begins with a conflict. This time, the conflict is not between a father and daughter, but a King and Queen.

options.text: Oberon wants Titania to marry Demetrius.
Titania is angry Oberon made her fall in love with Bottom.
Titania wants the magical potion from Oberon.
Titania won't give Oberon a little boy he wants.
Titania won't give Oberon Puck, his servant back.

starterQuiz.stem: In 'A Midsummer Night's Dream', what does Oberon do when Titania refuses to give him the little boy he wants?
starterQuiz.hint: Consider that although many characters do fall asleep in the play, they are not under a magical potion.
starterQuiz.feedback: After Titania refuses to give Oberon the little boy he wants, he states he will "torment" her. This "torment" comes in the form of putting a love potion on her so that she falls in love with the first person she sees.

options.text: He puts a sleeping potion on her.
He makes Bottom fall in love with her.
He turns her head into that of a donkey.
He puts a love potion on her.
He makes Demetrius and Lysander fall in love with her.

starterQuiz.stem: 'A Midsummer Night's Dream' is a play. Which of the following are features of plays?
starterQuiz.hint: Consider that although the supernatural features in 'A Midsummer Night's Dream', it does not have to feature in every play.
starterQuiz.feedback: When exploring 'A Midsummer Night's Dream', it is important to consider all of these aspects that make up a play. You can explore the dialogue, the stage directions, and the structure (via the creation of scenes).

starterQuiz.stem: In Act 2 of 'A Midsummer Night's Dream', the setting changes. How does the setting change?
starterQuiz.hint: Consider that although the characters remain on the same stage throughout, the setting does change. Different directors will choose how to present each setting by using props and staging.
starterQuiz.feedback: In Athens, there is order, stability and hierarchy. In the forest, there is much chaos and confusion. At the end of the play action returns to the city, perhaps suggesting order has been restored.

options.text: from a magical forest to Athens
the setting doesn't change - the characters are on the same stage
from Athens to a magical forest
from Theseus's court, to Egeus's house

exitQuiz.stem: In 'A Midsummer Night's Dream', what do the stage directions state Oberon and Titania have with them when they first appear on stage?
exitQuiz.hint: Consider that there is only one love potion in the play.
exitQuiz.feedback: The stage direction suggests both Oberon and Titania's status, but also their equality in terms of status.

exitQuiz.stem: In 'A Midsummer Night's Dream', what are some of the similarities between Titania and Hermia?
exitQuiz.hint: Consider that Hermia runs away to the magical forest after fleeing Athens.
exitQuiz.feedback: There are some key differences between Titania and Hermia in terms of their characterisation, but they are both in significant conflicts with important men in their lives.

options.text: they both fall in love with Bottom
they both live in the magical forest
they are both in conflict with a powerful man
they are both in conflict with their partner

exitQuiz.stem: {{}} are important to many play scripts. They are text in a play script which gives information about how a scene should be staged, or how an actor should say a particular line.
exitQuiz.hint: Consider this is a two word phrase. The second word can be a synonym for instructions.
exitQuiz.feedback: Just as you can explore dialogue when discussing or writing about a play, so too can you write about stage directions.

exitQuiz.stem: In Act 2 of 'A Midsummer Night's Dream', Oberon says to Titania, "I do but {{}} a little changeling boy/ To be my henchman".
exitQuiz.hint: Consider that this word means to ask, but suggests some sort of desperation.
exitQuiz.feedback: This could be performed in many different ways. An actor could convey some sort of desperation, or anger or a more sinister emotion conveying he will punish Titania if she doesn't agree to his demands.

exitQuiz.stem: In Act 2 of 'A Midsummer Night's Dream', after Titania leaves Oberon without giving him what he wants, he says "Thou shalt not from this grove [forest]/Till I {{}} thee for this injury."
exitQuiz.hint: Consider this word means to inflict pain - either physical or mental.
exitQuiz.feedback: Oberon makes it very clear that he seeks revenge on Titania for her refusal to give into his demand for the little boy. As soon as she leaves, he begins to enact his plan to use the magical potion on her.

exitQuiz.stem: In Act 2 of 'A Midsummer Night's Dream', when Oberon and Titania first enter, the stage directions read, "Enter Oberon the King of the Fairies, with his {{}}, and Titania [...] with hers."
exitQuiz.hint: Consider that this word means servants, followers or entourage.
exitQuiz.feedback: This stage directions reveals the power and might of the two monarchs in the forest. It also speaks to their equality, something that Hermia, in her conflict with her father, does not have.

starterQuiz.stem: In Act 2, Scene 1 of 'A Midsummer Night's Dream', Oberon asks Titania, "Am I not thy...?".
starterQuiz.hint: Consider this is a title for a man of high status.
starterQuiz.feedback: Oberon's question seems to be a challenge to Titania. He is her lord, and therefore, he feels, she should obey him.

starterQuiz.stem: In Act 2, Scene 1 of 'A Midsummer Night's Dream', Oberon asks Titania, "Am I not thy lord?". Titania replies, "Then I must be thy..."
starterQuiz.hint: Consider this is a title for a woman of high status.
starterQuiz.feedback: Titania's reply shows her equality with Oberon. She matches his statement like for like. She then enlarges on her answer, and in this way dominates the dialogue during this scene.

starterQuiz.stem: When Oberon and Titania first appear on stage in 'A Midsummer Night's Dream', Oberon calls Titania a "wanton". What does this word mean?
starterQuiz.hint: Consider that Oberon does call Titania "proud" but this is a different insult.
starterQuiz.feedback: Oberon believes that Titania is disobeying him, much like Egeus believes Hermia is disobeying him in Act 1.

exitQuiz.stem: In 'A Midsummer Night's Dream', why might we describe the character of Oberon as malevolent?
exitQuiz.hint: Consider this word means cruel or malicious.
exitQuiz.feedback: Shakespeare's Oberon is presented in many different ways. Sometimes he seems to want to help those around him, for example he wants to help Helena by making Demetrius fall in love with her. But his plan for Titania seems deliberately cruel.

options.text: he asks Titania to give him a little boy

exitQuiz.stem: In Act 2, Scene 1 of 'A Midsummer Night's Dream', what does Titania want to do as soon as she sees Oberon?
exitQuiz.hint: Consider that Titania is presented as powerful in this scene, and doesn't need to run away from Oberon.
exitQuiz.feedback: Titania says, "Fairies, skip hence." as her second sentence. She says she has sworn to stay away from Oberon because of his unreasonable demand that she give him the boy in her care.

exitQuiz.stem: When given a question about 'A Midsummer Night's Dream', you should annotate it. What kinds of notes might you annotate it with?
exitQuiz.hint: Consider that knowing the plot is important, but you don't need to include it in most questions about the play unless you are being asked for a summary of the story.
exitQuiz.feedback: Annotating an essay question is a short activity, but a crucial one. It makes sure that your thoughts are directed towards a certain aspect of the play, rather than everything you know about it. Annotating gives you a sense of purpose.

options.text: how an Elizabethan audience would answer the question
everything you know about the play

exitQuiz.stem: In 'A Midsummer Night's Dream', Oberon, just like Egeus, is in conflict with an important person in his life. What are other similarities between the two men?
exitQuiz.hint: Consider that whilst Egeus speaks more lines than Hermia when they are arguing, Titania dominates the dialogue with Oberon.
exitQuiz.feedback: Comparing the differences and similarities between the conflicts in Acts 1 and 2 can help understand each in more detail, particularly the power dynamics between the characters.

options.text: they both feel they are being disobeyed by women who should obey them
they both use the supernatural to punish the person they are arguing with
they both threaten to kill the person they are arguing with
they both ask someone to support them punishing the person they are fighting
they both dominate the dialogue when they talk to the person they are fighting

exitQuiz.stem: In Act 2, Scene 1 of 'A Midsummer Night's Dream', Oberon says, "Give me that boy" and Titania replies, "Not for thy ..."
exitQuiz.hint: Consider this is a two word phrase. It means the area over which Oberon rules.
exitQuiz.feedback: Oberon's demand is met with a flat refusal, and the phrase "fairy kingdom" shows just how valuable the boy is to Titania - she won't give him up for anything.

exitQuiz.stem: In Act 2, Scene 1 of 'A Midsummer Night's Dream', Titania says of Oberon, "I have {{}} his bed and company."
exitQuiz.hint: Consider this is an old fashioned word meaning to reject.
exitQuiz.feedback: Titania's second line shows her strong resolve not to engage with Oberon because of his demand for the boy. She seems to hold the power at this point, saying it is she who has decided that they will not see each other.
